D012-D021_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling constantly on edge for the past few months—ever since things started falling apart with the company. Lately, just the sight of storm clouds rolling in sends this wave of panic through me. My chest tightens, I can’t breathe, my heart races like I’m about to collapse. It doesn’t make sense—I’ve never been scared of thunderstorms before. But now, if I’m outside and the sky darkens, I have to get indoors immediately, even if it’s just a passing shower.  

Eating’s been… off, too. I don’t know why, but the thought of swallowing certain foods—especially anything thick or sticky—makes me feel like I’m going to choke. I’ve started cutting back, not because I want to lose weight or anything, but because I can’t shake the fear. It’s not about calories or shape; it’s like my body just revolts at the idea. I skip meals sometimes without noticing. I’m under so much stress I barely register hunger anymore.  

I can’t tell if this is all because I’m burning out or if something deeper’s wrong. The business is tanking, I’m alone most days, and I feel like I’m losing control—but over what, I can’t say.

A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Specific Phobia

    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

It’s not like I never eat those things—I do, but it takes real effort. I haven’t changed my weight much, and I don’t track calories obsessively. It’s just… the feeling creeps up, similar to how I feel around dogs—tight chest, dizzy, like I need to get out fast. It's been going on for a few months now, maybe longer.

    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
